subject: Meteorology
title: Cloud Classification System
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Cloud Classification System.

hook.text: In 1803, Luke Howard gave clouds Latin names—and his system is still used worldwide today.

buildup.text: Howard used three root forms: cumulus (heaped), stratus (layered), and cirrus (wispy/curled).

discovery.text: Prefixes mark altitude: cirro- for high, alto- for middle—and nimbo- or -nimbus signals rain-producing clouds.

twist.text: There are ten main cloud genera—every cloud you see fits into one of these ten official categories.

climax.text: The World Meteorological Organization maintains the International Cloud Atlas—the definitive cloud guide.

punchline.text: Ten names cover every cloud in the sky—not bad for 1803.

quiz.question: Who created the cloud naming system still used today?
